title: Order Granting Waiver Request re Foundry Works Solar Energy LLC under ER26-3713.

197 FERC ¶ 61,055
UNITED STATES OF AMERICA
FEDERAL ENERGY REGULATORY COMMISSION

Before Commissioners:  Laura V. Swett, Chairman;
                                        David Rosner, Lindsay S. See,
                                        Judy W. Chang, and David LaCerte.


ORDER GRANTING WAIVER REQUEST

(Issued October 23, 2026)

On September 3, 2026, pursuant to Rules 207(a)(5) and 212 of the Commission’s Rules of Practice and Procedure, Foundry Works Solar Energy LLC (Foundry Works) filed a request for waiver of:  (1) section 4.4.4 of Attachment X (Generator Interconnection Procedures (GIP)) of Midcontinent Independent System Operator, Inc.’s (MISO) Open Access Transmission, Energy and Operating Reserve Markets Tariff (Tariff); and 
(2) Article 2.3.1 of the Amended and Restated Generator Interconnection Agreement (GIA) among Foundry Works as interconnection customer, Northern Indiana Public Service Company LLC (NIPSCO) as transmission owner, and MISO as transmission provider (Foundry Works GIA).  Foundry Works requests that the Commission grant waiver to allow for a one-year extension of the commercial operation deadline for its battery energy storage system (BESS) (Project), from December 15, 2027, to December 15, 2028.  As discussed below, we grant Foundry Works’ waiver request.  
Background
GIP section 4.4.4 provides, in relevant part, that:
Consistent with Article 2.3.1 of the GIA, once that GIA is executed or filed unexecuted, if the Generating Facility fails to reach Commercial Operation by the Commercial Operation Date set forth in the GIA, such Commercial Operation Date as set forth in the GIA may be extended by Interconnection Customer for a period up to three (3) consecutive years, after which Transmission Provider shall terminate the GIA if the Generating Facility has still failed to reach Commercial Operation.
Article 2.3.1 of the Foundry Works GIA provides, in relevant part, that:
This GIA shall be terminated by Transmission Provider if the Generating Facility or a portion of the Generating Facility fails to achieve Commercial Operation by the Commercial Operation Date established in accordance with Section 4.4.4 of Attachment X, including any extension provided thereunder . . . .
Appendix B of the Foundry Works GIA establishes milestones for the interconnection of the Project, including a commercial operation date of December 15, 2024.  Pursuant to GIP section 4.4.4 and Article 2.3.1 of the Foundry Works GIA, MISO must terminate the Foundry Works GIA if the Project does not achieve commercial operation by December 15, 2027.
Foundry Works states that it is developing the Project, a 200 MW BESS in Lake County, Indiana, that will interconnect to the transmission system owned by NIPSCO and operated by MISO.  Foundry Works explains that it has been diligently pursuing the Project’s development and that it has spent $38 million, secured 100% of the land rights, conducted design and engineering studies for a BESS facility, rezoned the property, and funded all network upgrades, which are under construction and nearly complete.  Foundry Works further states that it has purchased equipment with long-lead times, including the main power transformers.
Foundry Works states that, on October 15, 2025, it submitted a generator replacement request to MISO to effectuate a fuel change from a 200 MW solar generating facility to a 200 MW BESS.  Foundry Works explains that this change is responsive to unanticipated and significant resource adequacy challenges facing its region due to the addition of data centers and other large loads.  Foundry Works states that it has received MISO’s approval and completed all studies for the BESS facility.  Foundry Works states that Indianapolis Power & Light Company d/b/a AES Indiana (AES Indiana) has executed an agreement to purchase Foundry Works and use the Project to serve AES Indiana’s load.  
Foundry Works states that it is currently preparing an application for a BESS special exception permit and anticipates that the permitting process will be completed by the fourth quarter of 2026.  Additionally, Foundry Works states that it will thereafter obtain the remaining administrative construction permits by the first quarter of 2027, after which it plans to commence the Project’s construction in Spring 2027.  Foundry Works states that construction will take approximately 12-16 months, and testing and commissioning will take an additional three to six months.  Foundry Works states that, based on that development and construction timeline, it will not meet the commercial operation deadline of December 15, 2027, but it expects the Project will achieve commercial operation by December 15, 2028. 
Waiver Request
Foundry Works requests waiver of GIP section 4.4.4 and Article 2.3.1 of the Foundry Works GIA to allow for a one-year extension of the commercial operation deadline for the Project, from December 15, 2027, to December 15, 2028.  Foundry Works asserts that its waiver request satisfies the Commission’s criteria for granting waiver.
First, Foundry Works argues that it acted in good faith to diligently advance the Project.  Foundry Works contends that it has been actively developing the Project, but recent resource adequacy challenges created circumstances beyond its control that warranted the change to a BESS to better serve utilities’ data center load.  Foundry Works further asserts that it has acted in good faith to meet the region’s and AES Indiana’s capacity needs by significantly progressing the Project while working with MISO and NIPSCO to coordinate the generator replacement process and ensure that all of its financial obligations under the Foundry Works GIA are met under the originally contemplated schedule.  Foundry Works states that it has fully funded the Project’s network upgrades and made other significant investments totaling approximately 
$38 million.  Foundry Works explains that, consistent with Commission precedent, 
it has acted in good faith by spending significant resources, time, and effort in developing the Project.
Second, Foundry Works asserts that the requested relief is of limited scope because it requests waiver of only those Tariff provisions necessary to permit a one-year extension of the commercial operation deadline.  Additionally, Foundry Works states that the requested waiver would not relieve Foundry Works of any financial requirements nor provide for an open-ended schedule extension.  Finally, Foundry Works states that the request is tailored to the amount of time it will take Foundry Works to finish development and construction of the Project.
Third, Foundry Works argues that the requested relief addresses a concrete problem by ensuring that the Project will have sufficient time to complete construction without having the Foundry Works GIA terminated.  Foundry Works states that it is actively developing the Project and has obtained completed generator replacement studies from MISO.  However, Foundry Works asserts that it needs approximately 18-24 months to complete the development and construction process after it receives BESS permits, which it estimates it will receive in the first quarter of 2027.  As such, it will not meet the current commercial operation deadline, but it expects the Project to achieve commercial operation by December 15, 2028.
Finally, Foundry Works argues that the requested waiver will not have undesirable consequences, such as harming third parties.  Foundry Works states that it has funded its network upgrades, which are under construction; thus, no other interconnection customer will be harmed by granting the waiver request.  Foundry Works asserts that, to the contrary, granting a waiver will benefit third parties by enabling AES Indiana to reliably serve its growing load, thereby alleviating the strain of increased demand on the system and reducing the risk of supply shortfalls and instability.
Foundry Works states that it is authorized to represent that MISO supports and NIPSCO does not oppose the waiver request.  Foundry Works asserts that the Commission’s timely action on the waiver request is critical to allow Foundry Works and AES Indiana the ability to satisfy a November 1, 2026 contractual milestone under their agreement, preserve the Project’s continued commercial viability, and ensure its ability to support the resource adequacy needs of AES Indiana’s service territory.  
Notice and Responsive Pleadings
Notice of Foundry Works’ filing was published in the Federal Register, 91 Fed. Reg. 57588 (Sep. 10, 2026), with interventions and protests due on or before September 24, 2026.  MISO filed a timely motion to intervene.  Just Transition Northwest Indiana (JTNWI) filed comments.  On September 30, 2026, AES Indiana filed an out-of-time motion to intervene and comments.  On October 2, 2026, Foundry Works filed an answer to JTNWI’s comments.
JTNWI’s Comments
JTNWI states that, while it supports responsible battery storage when lawfully permitted, it provides additional information for the Commission’s consideration that appears absent from Foundry Works’ waiver request.  Specifically, JTNWI states that consideration of the BESS special exception was deferred by the Lake County Planning Commission until October 2026.  JTNWI further states that commercial operation of the Project also depends on local land use authorization for the Dinwiddie substation, which will serve as the Project’s point of interconnection, but NIPSCO has not yet applied for the necessary special exception.  JTNWI asserts that these facts call into question the development timeline presented in the waiver request.  JTNWI also states that residents have reported county stop-work action related to the substation construction, and that county counsel has acknowledged resident statements about the sequencing of substation construction relative to the required local approvals.  JTNWI also addresses Foundry Works’ assertion that delays in project development are due to factors beyond its control.  JTNWI states that the Project entered the interconnection queue in 2018 as a solar resource, Foundry Works requested replacement with battery storage in late 2025, and the rezoning was approved on June 9, 2026, substantially later than the Project’s queue entry.  Further, JTNWI asserts that in another proceeding involving AES Indiana’s Monrovia Project, witness testimony noted that “Foundry [Works] was seeking federal flexibility toward 2029.”  JTNWI notes that other generation and storage projects are planned to interconnect at the same substation, including separate battery storage in MISO’s queue.  JTNWI questions whether shared substation construction sequencing affects the realism of a December 15, 2028 commercial operation deadline.
AES Indiana’s Comments
AES Indiana states that it supports Foundry Works’ waiver request.  AES Indiana asserts that Foundry Works meets the Commission’s standard for waiver requests and that granting the waiver request would provide Foundry Works with the time to secure all necessary local permits and to complete construction of the Project, which has become delayed due to reasons outside of Foundry Works’ control.  AES Indiana asserts that the executed purchase agreement between AES Indiana and Foundry Works is evidence of Foundry Works’ good faith and diligent commitment to developing the Project and that the Project is not speculative or unsupported.  In addition, AES Indiana states that Foundry Works asks for a limited and tailored amount of time to complete the permitting and construction process.  Further, AES Indiana asserts that the waiver request is specific and would address the concrete problem that Foundry Works is unable to meet the current commercial operation deadline.  Finally, AES agrees with Foundry Works that granting the waiver request would not result in harm to third parties or have any adverse impact on the transmission system.  AES Indiana states that, instead, granting the waiver request would bring Foundry Works closer to contributing capacity needed to meet demand in Indiana and ensure reliable, affordable energy for AES Indiana’s customers.
Foundry Works’ Answer
Foundry Works states that nothing in JTNWI’s comments negates Foundry Works’ showing that the Commission should grant the requested waiver.  Foundry Works reiterates that circumstances outside its control, including construction timelines, permitting timelines, and changes to the resource adequacy environment make the waiver request necessary.  Specifically, Foundry Works asserts that it changed the Project from a solar facility to a BESS in response to critical resource adequacy challenges in the MISO region and due to the North American Electric Reliability Corporation classifying the Midwest region as “high risk” beginning in 2028.  In support of this facility change, Foundry Works explains that it successfully rezoned the Project site for BESS use as of June 9, 2026, and it is currently pursuing the BESS special exception permit in late 2026, with final construction permits anticipated to be issued in early 2027, after which construction can commence.  Foundry Works avers that, contrary to JTNWI’s claims that pending land use approvals do not demonstrate project readiness, approvals remaining in progress is entirely consistent with the orderly, sequential permitting timelines set forth in the waiver request.  Further, Foundry Works contends that the deferral referenced by JTNWI was to provide Foundry Works additional time to work on routine engineering and mitigation plans that will be presented to the Lake County Planning Commission on October 21, 2026 and that these are standard permitting steps.
Foundry Works further asserts that JTNWI’s concerns about local permits and construction timelines are misplaced.  First, Foundry Works contends that the Commission routinely grants commercial operation deadline waivers where permits are pending and construction is ongoing.  Second, Foundry Works states that JTNWI’s concerns that NIPSCO has not yet submitted the special exception request for the Dinwiddie Substation are misplaced because Foundry Works cannot exercise control 
over NIPSCO’s work on its substation.  Foundry Works states that NIPSCO has already completed 90-95% of the substation work and plans to submit the special exception application on or about October 10, 2026.  Foundry Works asserts that there is no reason to believe that any work NIPSCO does for other interconnection customers will impact Foundry Works’ ability to achieve commercial operation of its Project by December 15, 2028.
Discussion
Procedural Matters
Pursuant to Rule 214 of the Commission’s Rules of Practice and Procedure, 
18 C.F.R. § 385.214 (2025), MISO’s timely, unopposed motion to intervene serves to make it a party to this proceeding.
Pursuant to Rule 214(d) of the Commission’s Rules of Practice and Procedure, 
18 C.F.R. § 385.214(d), we grant AES Indiana’s late-filed motion to intervene given its interest in the proceeding, the early stage of the proceeding, and the absence of undue prejudice or delay.
Rule 213(a)(2) of the Commission’s Rules of Practice and Procedure, 18 C.F.R. § 385.213(a)(2) (2025), prohibits an answer to a protest unless otherwise ordered by the decisional authority.  We accept Foundry Works’ answer because it has provided information that assisted us in our decision-making process.
Substantive Matters 
We grant Foundry Works’ waiver request.  Specifically, we grant Foundry Works’ request for waiver of GIP section 4.4.4 and Article 2.3.1 of the Foundry Works GIA to allow for a one-year extension of the commercial operation deadline for the Project, from December 15, 2027, to December 15, 2028.  The Commission has granted waiver of 
tariff provisions where:  (1) the applicant acted in good faith; (2) the waiver is limited
 in scope; (3) the waiver addresses a concrete problem; and (4) the waiver does not 
have undesirable consequences, such as harming third parties.  We find that the circumstances of Foundry Works’ waiver request satisfy these criteria. 
First, we find that Foundry Works has acted in good faith to develop the Project in accordance with the GIP and the Foundry Works GIA.  Foundry Works states that it has made significant progress in reaching its milestones required under the Foundry Works GIA, has invested $38 million to develop the Project, secured 100% of the land rights, funded all network upgrades, conducted engineering and design work, and purchased equipment with long-lead times, including the main power transformers.  Foundry Works further states that it has executed an agreement that will allow AES Indiana to support its urgent resource adequacy needs.  Additionally, Foundry Works states that it has worked with MISO and NIPSCO to coordinate the generator replacement process and ensure that all of its financial obligations under the Foundry Works GIA are met under the originally contemplated schedule.
Second, we find that the requested waiver is of limited scope because it represents a one-time waiver of GIP section 4.4.4 and Article 2.3.1 of the Foundry Works GIA to allow for a one-year extension of the commercial operation deadline for the Project, 
from December 15, 2027, to December 15, 2028.  The limited waiver applies only to 
this deadline and does not relieve Foundry Works of any financial requirements in the Foundry Works GIA.  Further, if the Project does not achieve commercial operation by December 15, 2028, the Foundry Works GIA will be subject to termination by MISO. 
With regard to JTNWI’s generalized statements that ongoing permitting proceedings and local land-use considerations call into question Foundry Works’ suggested timeline, we find that Foundry Works has provided a sufficient explanation on the timeline that it believes would allow the Project to feasibly finish development and construction of the Project.  Specifically, Foundry Works states that it anticipates obtaining a special exception permit by the fourth quarter of 2026 and remaining administrative construction permits by the first quarter of 2027, after which it plans to commence the Project’s construction in Spring 2027.  In response to JTNWI’s observation that the special exception was deferred until October 2026, Foundry Works states that the deferral was intended to provide Foundry Works additional time to prepare for presentation to the Lake County Planning Commission, and Foundry Works does not anticipate that consideration of the local land approvals will affect the overall permitting schedule.  Further, Foundry Works explains that construction will take approximately 12-16 months, and testing and commissioning will take an additional three to six months.
Third, we find that granting the waiver will remedy a concrete problem.  Absent waiver, MISO must terminate the Foundry Works GIA if the Project does not achieve commercial operation by the December 15, 2027 deadline.  However, Foundry Works states that the Project is unable to achieve commercial operation by December 15, 2027.  We find that granting waiver will provide Foundry Works with the additional time needed to obtain the required permitting, complete the construction of the Project, and achieve commercial operation by December 15, 2028.
Finally, we find that the requested waiver will not have undesirable consequences, such as harming third parties.  Foundry Works represents that it has fully funded its network upgrades, and therefore no other interconnection customer will be harmed by granting the waiver request.
The Commission orders: 

Foundry Works’ waiver request is hereby granted, as discussed in the body of this order.

By the Commission.

( S E A L )




Debbie-Anne A. Reese,
Secretary.
